question: The amount on a sum of ₹2,500 at the rate of 14% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective compound interest rate for 2 years can be found using the successive percentage change formula.

⇒ Effective Rate = X + Y + (X × Y)/100

⇒ Effective Rate = 14 + 14 + (14 × 14)/100 = 28 + 1.96 = 29.96%

⇒ Total Amount = 129.96% of 2500

⇒ Total Amount = 1.2996 × 2500 = 3249

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,249.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Compound Interest Rate

For 2 years at a rate of R% per annum, the effective compound interest rate is calculated using the successive percentage formula: [2R + R²/100]%.

Difference Between CI and SI

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for exactly 2 years on a principal P at rate R% is given directly by the formula: P(R/100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

When compound interest is calculated half-yearly, the annual interest rate is halved (R/2) and the number of compounding periods is doubled (2n).
